ⓘ How unit-of-measure (UoM) conversion works

Suppliers don't always quote in the same unit the buyer asks for. Before any prices can be compared fairly, every quote is converted to the buyer's UoM for that item.

The rule

Each line is normalised so the unit price and demand are in the same unit:

normalised unit price = supplier unit price × (supplier UoM → buyer UoM factor)

Example

Buyer wants 500 M (metres) of cable. Supplier quotes $12 per FT (foot).

1 M = 3.281 FT → $12/FT × 3.281 = $39.37 / M
line cost = $39.37 × 500 M = $19,685

Suppliers are only ranked against each other after this conversion — otherwise a cheaper-looking unit could just be a smaller unit.

Pack / lot sizes

If a supplier sells only in packs (e.g. boxes of 100), the price is divided down to the single buyer unit first, then the MoQ and lot-size rules are applied on top (see the Apply MoQ logic switch).
